source.citation: Sources read but not reconstructed as scored fixtures; kept so the reasons stay with the data.

fixtures.source: Xing C-Y et al. Front Physiol 2021;12:672351, doi 10.3389/fphys.2021.672351, Tables 1-3 and Fig 2 (full text read)
fixtures.observed: Tilt table, 20 men. Heart-level mean pressure 93 +/- 6 mmHg at baseline, 69 +/- 9 in the first 5 s back at +1 g after 15 s at -0.87 g, then about 75 and 84 (Fig 2). Cerebral flow velocity -7.8 +/- 4.4 cm/s (-13%), back by 10 s.
fixtures.reason: No control without the push, so the dip mixes push-pull with the change of posture; time zero relative to the 3.3 s tilt is not given; no visual or LOC events were monitored. Compared qualitatively with the Perfusion model's heart-level pressure, not scored.

fixtures.source: Houghton JO et al. Aviat Space Environ Med 1985;56:956-965, PMID 4062770 (abstract)
fixtures.observed: n 8: '2- and 4-s onset' to 6.1 g, absolute incapacitation 12.1 s; 0.067 g/s to 7.2 g, 16.6 s.
fixtures.reason: The rapid onset is ambiguous, protection and offsets are not given, and there are no spreads.

fixtures.source: Whinnery JE, Whinnery AM. Arch Neurol 1990;47:764-776, PMID 2357157 (abstract)
fixtures.observed: 501 episodes: absolute incapacitation 11.9 s, relative 16 s, total 28 s.
fixtures.reason: Pooled over unreported profiles; overlaps the W14 population.

fixtures.source: Copeland K. CGEM user's guide, DOT/FAA/AM-23/5, Appendices B-D; Copeland and Whinnery, DOT/FAA/AM-23/6, Figs 1-2
fixtures.observed: Model outputs: a 27-rate series for an average woman and a vertical-eight run (visual onset 27.509 s at 5.902 g, blackout 29.406 s at 4.535 g, no G-LOC).
fixtures.reason: Golden traces of the CGEM model, not human data. The CGEM software's licence and source are unknown, so no Reference model was built; these would test one.
